chunks.title: Name and boilerplate
chunks.text:
# Name and boilerplate — University name

On first reference, use the full name University of Illinois Chicago. On second reference, UIC is acceptable. Do not use a comma or the word "at" in the university name, and never write U of I Chicago or UI-Chicago. Do not use "the" before UIC when it stands alone.

chunks.title: Name and boilerplate
chunks.text:
# Name and boilerplate — Boilerplate

Use the approved boilerplate at the end of news releases: UIC is Chicago's only public research university, with 16 colleges and more than 34,000 students. Do not edit the boilerplate text.

chunks.title: Voice and tone
chunks.text:
# Voice and tone — Brand attributes

UIC's voice is bold, authentic and welcoming. We write with confidence but without exaggeration. Use clear, concise sentences and active verbs. Avoid jargon, cliches and excessive exclamation points.

chunks.title: Voice and tone
chunks.text:
# Voice and tone — Tone and readability

Write in plain language at a conversational tone. Prefer short sentences and simple, familiar words so messages are readable by a broad audience. Aim for roughly an eighth-grade reading level.

chunks.title: Brand strategy
chunks.text:
# Brand strategy — Students

Key audience: prospective and current students. Messages should emphasize access, opportunity and a supportive community in the heart of Chicago, and speak to students directly about next steps.

chunks.title: Brand strategy
chunks.text:
# Brand strategy — Faculty and staff

Key audience: faculty and staff. Messaging highlights research excellence, collaboration across disciplines and pride in the campus community. Use a collegial, informative tone with colleagues.

chunks.title: Editorial and style guide
chunks.text:
# Editorial and style guide — Dates and times

Abbreviate the months Jan., Feb., Aug., Sept., Oct., Nov. and Dec. when used with a specific date. Spell out March, April, May, June and July. Use a.m. and p.m. in lowercase with periods; use noon and midnight instead of 12 p.m. and 12 a.m. Do not use ordinals such as 1st or 2nd with dates.

chunks.title: Editorial and style guide
chunks.text:
# Editorial and style guide — Academic titles

Capitalize formal titles such as professor, dean or chancellor only when they appear directly before a name. Lowercase titles that follow a name or stand alone. Use Dr. only for medical doctors on first reference.

chunks.title: Editorial and style guide
chunks.text:
# Editorial and style guide — Accessibility

Link text must describe the destination; do not use click here or read more. Every meaningful image needs alternative text, and videos require captions. Use headings in order so screen reader users can navigate.

chunks.title: Editorial and style guide
chunks.text:
# Editorial and style guide — Inclusive language

Use gender-neutral language: chair instead of chairman, first-year student instead of freshman, and they as a singular pronoun instead of he or she. Use person-first language, such as a person with a disability.
